sample_unit: patients (421 AP knee radiographs; 128 fracture patients in the main six-class analysis)

links.outcome: Whether archive-assembly artifacts (accompanying CT section) leak label information and inflate benchmark performance
links.effect: Fracture vs no classifiable fracture: network 0.833 vs 0.814 for a no-pixel model (p=0.264); coronal CT section accompanied 126/128 fracture patients but 24/58 others (p=2.9e-19).
links.quote: a coronal computed tomography section accompanied 126 of 128 fracture patients but 24 of 58 others (p = 2.9 × 10-19)

unlisted_practices: Negative-control baselines fitted with no pixel content (metadata/non-anatomical regression) to test whether benchmark accuracy exceeds shortcuts
Ablation paired with its complement (tibia-only input) to localize where the signal lies
Patient-grouped stratified cross-validation with multiple seeds and balanced accuracy

screen.reason: Evaluates and tests a transferable diagnostic auditing/control protocol (ablation, non-anatomical baselines, augmentation audit) to identify confounding, shortcut learning, and archive bias prior to deployment.

primary.practice: benchmark control protocol / shortcut and confounding audit
